standard.title: Investigate media artists
standard.description: investigate the ways that media artists use media arts concepts to construct representations in media arts works and practices across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can compare media representations across contexts and explain how context shapes values and stereotypes. They have analysed power relationships in representations. They have not yet investigated at the level of evaluating social, cultural and ethical implications — or analysing how media platforms use data to shape audience information.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate how media artists use media arts concepts to construct representations across cultures, times, places and contexts — evaluating social, cultural and ethical implications and how audiences are positioned.

nodes.label: Technical and symbolic codes — ideology and positioning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse how technical and symbolic codes communicate social beliefs, values and ideology — and evaluate how audiences are positioned to respond.
nodes.minimum_width: Analyse how at least three technical or symbolic codes in a media arts work communicate specific social beliefs or values, and explain how the work positions its audience to respond.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how social beliefs and values are communicated through technical and symbolic codes; evaluate how audiences are positioned by representations; investigate stereotypical representations across historical and contemporary contexts; examine how media institutions and practices influence audience perceptions.
wider: Analyse and evaluate how a specific media arts genre has communicated and evolved its ideological positioning across different historical periods — identifying the technical and symbolic code changes that correspond to social changes, and evaluating what this reveals about media's relationship to ideology

Investigate how media platforms use data to influence the breadth and depth of information provided to audiences — examining algorithmic curation through media feeds and evaluating the implications for audience agency, representation and ideological positioning
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding how codes communicate ideology and position audiences is the conceptual foundation for this standard at Y9-10 — without it, subsequent evaluation of social, cultural and ethical implications has no analytical grounding.

response_modes.reason: Students need an explicit analytical framework: 'What values does this code communicate? Who is positioned to agree with this representation? Whose perspective is marginalised?' This is the critical media literacy reasoning chain at Y9-10.

success_criteria: Student can analyse how at least three technical or symbolic codes in a media arts work communicate social beliefs or values
Student can explain how the work positions its audience to respond and whose perspectives are centred or marginalised

nodes.label: Social, cultural and ethical implications
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate the social, cultural and ethical implications of representations in media arts works — including how representations have changed over time and how media practices perpetuate or challenge prevailing views.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate the social, cultural or ethical implications of representations in one media arts context — identifying what prevailing views are communicated and what the implications are for the groups represented.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse and evaluate how representations have changed over time (e.g. gender, multiculturalism, youth in Australian media); research audiences of specific genres and evaluate how codes engage them across media forms; examine the role of media makers in perpetuating and/or challenging prevailing views; justify creative choices in video commentary form.
wider: Analyse and evaluate the social, cultural and ethical implications of changing representations in Australian media over time — deconstructing representations of gender, multiculturalism or youth across decades, evaluating the social forces that shaped each period, and assessing the cumulative impact

Produce a video commentary justifying the technical and symbolic code choices made in an original work — explaining the social and cultural value framework behind choices, communicating alternative points of view, and evaluating how effectively the work challenges prevailing representations

response_modes.reason: Vary the evaluation contexts — different representation categories, different time periods, different media forms — to ensure students develop genuine evaluative range rather than applying a single analytical lens to a single context.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of social, cultural and ethical evaluation contexts at Y9-10 (gender, multiculturalism, youth, First Nations, algorithmic curation, media institution power) is genuinely rich — students who evaluate across multiple contexts develop much stronger critical media literacy.
success_criteria: Student evaluates the social, cultural or ethical implications of representations in at least one media arts context
Student can explain what prevailing views are communicated and what the implications are for the groups represented
